nodes.summary: On `(0, 1)` the current `J = σ F - F' / 2` of the stationary forward equation, for the weighted density `F(x) = x (1 - x) φ(x)`, is the constant `θ · u_σ'(0) / 2` (`u_σ'(0) = kimuraSlope σ = 2σ / (1 - e^{-2σ})`, and `1` for `σ = 0`), so `J = θ σ / (1 - e^{-2σ})`, and `J = θ / 2` in the neutral case: the mutational input of frequency at `0`, carried through `(0, 1)` to fixation at `1`.
nodes.title: Probability current

nodes.summary: Let `θ ≠ 0` and let `φ` be a density on `(0, 1)` whose weighted density `x (1 - x) φ(x)` extends to a function `F` continuous on `[0, 1]`, twice differentiable on `(0, 1)`, solving the stationary forward equation `½ F'' - σ F' = 0` there, with boundary normalizations `F(0) = θ` and `F(1) = 0`. Then `φ` is the Sawyer–Hartl density on `(0, 1)`.
nodes.title: ODE characterization of the Poisson-random-field density

nodes.summary: With `σ = 0` the expected number of sites at which all `n ≥ 1` sampled copies carry the derived allele is `θ / n`. These sites are monomorphic in the sample, so this is not a class of the site-frequency spectrum.
nodes.title: Expected number of sites derived in the whole neutral sample

nodes.summary: With `σ = 0`, for the segregating classes `1 ≤ i < n` the expected number of sites with `i` derived copies in a sample of `n` is `θ / i`.
nodes.title: Neutral site-frequency spectrum (Fu 1995)

nodes.summary: The expected unfolded site-frequency spectrum of a sample of `n` gene copies under the Poisson random field: the expected number of sites where exactly `i` of the `n` sampled copies carry the derived allele, `E ξ_i = ∫ x in 0..1, C(n, i) x ^ i (1 - x) ^ (n - i) φ(x)`. The site-frequency spectrum consists of the segregating classes `1 ≤ i < n`. The value at `i = n` is the expected number of sites at which every…
nodes.title: Expected site frequency spectrum under the Poisson random field

nodes.summary: On `(0, 1)` the weighted density `F(x) = x (1 - x) φ(x)` of the Poisson-random-field density solves the stationary Fokker–Planck equation `½ F'' - σ F' = 0` of the Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection `σ` (the forward equation `½ (x (1 - x) φ)'' - (σ x (1 - x) φ)' = 0`).
nodes.title: Stationary forward equation (Sawyer–Hartl 1992)

nodes.summary: The Poisson-random-field density with selection, explicitly: `θ (1 - e^{-2σ(1 - x)}) / ((1 - e^{-2σ}) x (1 - x))` for `σ ≠ 0`.
nodes.title: Closed form of the Poisson random field density with selection

nodes.summary: A new neutral mutation enters at a small frequency `p`; with mutations arriving at rate `θ / (2p)` per unit time (so that the mutational input of frequency is `θ / 2`), the expected sojourn density at `x ≥ p` is `θ / (2p) · G(p, x) = θ / x`, the neutral Poisson-random-field density.
nodes.title: The neutral density from the Green's function

nodes.summary: The neutral Poisson-random-field density is `θ / x` (for `x ≠ 1`).
nodes.title: Neutral Poisson random field density

nodes.summary: The Sawyer–Hartl (1992) Poisson-random-field density: the expected number of sites per unit frequency at which the derived allele has frequency `x`, for scaled mutation rate `θ = 4Nu` and scaled genic selection `σ = 2Ns`: `θ · u_σ(1 - x) / (x (1 - x))` with `u_σ = kimuraFixation σ`, i.e. `θ (1 - e^{-2σ(1 - x)}) / ((1 - e^{-2σ}) x (1 - x))`, and `θ / x` when `σ = 0`. The model domain is `θ > 0` and `x ∈ (0, 1)`; at…
nodes.title: Sawyer–Hartl Poisson random field density

nodes.summary: As `x → 1⁻` the weighted density `x (1 - x) φ(x)` tends to `0`.
nodes.title: Boundary normalization at `1`

nodes.summary: As `x → 0⁺` the weighted density `x (1 - x) φ(x)` tends to `θ`. (This is not the probability current, which is `current_prfDensity`.)
nodes.title: Boundary normalization at `0`

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
